raw_response:
I've been farming this land for 45 years. My mother farmed it before me. I don't need to think too hard about this — my hands know what to do with wheat and maize in Quzhou. The land is the same land, same well, same seasons. Two mouths to feed, 12 mu to work. My son-in-law sometimes helps with the heavy machinery.

**Wheat first** — I put in winter wheat every October after the maize comes off. All 12 mu goes to wheat. I've always used the improved seed from the village cooperative — the old varieties got disease and we stopped growing them years ago. I do three or four waterings: once when I sow and the seedlings establish, once in spring when they green up, once at jointing, and once at heading if the weather is dry. Four times is safe. I split my urea — put base fertilizer down with the phosphate before sowing, then top-dress in spring. I spray for weeds in winter and spray for aphids and rust before heading. I plough before sowing wheat because the maize stalks need turning under. I expect about 450 jin per mu — that's what I usually get.

**Maize second** — Right after wheat harvest in June I plant maize on the same 12 mu. No time to waste, the season is short. I use hybrid seed, everyone in the village does now, it yields much better. I don't plough — I just do rotary tillage to break up the surface, it's faster and the soil is already loose enough. I put fertilizer down at planting and top-dress when the plant is knee-high. Maize doesn't need as much water from the well if the summer rains come, but I'll irrigate at least twice — once at emergence if it's dry, and once at silking. I spray once or twice for corn borer and sometimes for weeds early on. I expect around 600 jin per mu.
